title: Leaving out words after auxiliary verbs
summary: Опущение слов после вспомогательных глаголов (I can't, but she can), so / neither + aux + S, запрет сокращения в конце фразы, британское do.
ru:
## Идея: оставляем только вспомогательный глагол
Чтобы не повторять уже известное, после **вспомогательного или модального глагола** остальная часть сказуемого опускается, если из контекста ясно, что имелось в виду.
> A: Have you finished? B: Yes, I **have**. — Да.
> She can't swim, but her brother **can**. — ...а её брат умеет.
> He said he would call, and he **did**.
> I'd help you if I **could**.
В русском ту же роль играет «да / умею / сделал»; в английском нужен именно **вспомогательный глагол** в правильном времени и лице, а не просто *yes*.

## Какой глагол оставить
| В первой части | Что остаётся | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| модальный (can, will, should) | тот же модальный | I can't come, but Tom **can**. |
| have / has + V3 | have / has | I haven't been there, but she **has**. |
| be (глагол и вспомогательный) | be | He isn't tired, but I **am**. |
| простое время, без вспомогательного | **do / does / did** | She doesn't swim, but he **does**. |
Если оригинал был сложным (*might have been waiting*), обычно оставляют **первый** вспомогательный или первые два: *A: Could she have been lost? B: She might (have).* Форма вспомогательного может отличаться от первой части: *I didn't phone, but I **should have**.*

## Нельзя: краткая форма в конце
Если вспомогательный стоит **последним** в предложении, его нельзя сокращать (на конце ударение).
- ~~Yes, I've.~~ → Yes, I **have**.
- ~~Is he coming? I think he's.~~ → I think he **is**.
- ~~Tom's tired, and I'm.~~ → ...and I **am**.
Отрицательные краткие формы допустимы: *No, I haven't. · No, he isn't.*

## so, neither, nor + вспомогательный + подлежащее
Так мы соглашаемся: **so + aux + S** (утверждение) и **neither / nor + aux + S** (отрицание). Вспомогательный должен соответствовать глаголу исходной фразы.
> A: I love hiking. B: So **do** I. — Я тоже.
> A: She's very talented. B: So **is** her brother.
> A: I haven't seen it. B: Neither **have** I. / Nor **have** I.
> A: He can't cook. B: Neither **can** I.
Параллельно: *I do too. · I don't either. · Me too. · Me neither.* (разговорно).
Важное различие: **So it is / So I did** (подлежащее перед вспомогательным) — не согласие, а **подтверждение**, часто с лёгким удивлением: *A: It's freezing. B: So it is!*

## Британский вариант с do
В британском английском после модального глагола можно оставить **do**: *A: Are you going? B: I might **do**. · I haven't seen it, but I should **do**.* В американском английском так не говорят.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~Do you like it? — Yes, I like.~~ → Yes, I **do**.
- ~~She hasn't called, and neither she has.~~ → ...and neither **has** her sister.
- ~~I can't swim and neither I can.~~ → ...and neither **can** I.
- ~~A: I'm tired. B: So I do.~~ → So **am** I.
en:
## The idea: keep only the auxiliary
To avoid repeating what is already clear, we can leave out everything after an **auxiliary or modal verb**.
> A: Have you finished? B: Yes, I **have**.
> She can't swim, but her brother **can**.
> He said he would call, and he **did**.
> I'd help you if I **could**.
In Russian "да / умеет / сделал" would do; in English you need an auxiliary in the right tense and person, not just *yes*.

## Which verb stays
| In the first part | What stays | Example |
|---|---|---|
| modal (can, will, should) | the same modal | I can't come, but Tom **can**. |
| have / has + past participle | have / has | I haven't been there, but she **has**. |
| be (main verb or auxiliary) | be | He isn't tired, but I **am**. |
| simple tense, no auxiliary | **do / does / did** | She doesn't swim, but he **does**. |
If the original was complex (*might have been waiting*), we usually keep the **first** auxiliary or the first two: *A: Could she have been lost? B: She might (have).* The auxiliary may differ from the first part: *I didn't phone, but I **should have**.*

## Not allowed: a contraction at the end
An auxiliary at the very end of a clause is stressed and cannot be contracted.
- ~~Yes, I've.~~ → Yes, I **have**.
- ~~Is he coming? I think he's.~~ → I think he **is**.
- ~~Tom's tired, and I'm.~~ → ...and I **am**.
Negative contractions are fine: *No, I haven't. · No, he isn't.*

## so, neither, nor + auxiliary + subject
We agree with **so + aux + S** (positive) and **neither / nor + aux + S** (negative). The auxiliary matches the original verb.
> A: I love hiking. B: So **do** I.
> A: She's very talented. B: So **is** her brother.
> A: I haven't seen it. B: Neither **have** I. / Nor **have** I.
> A: He can't cook. B: Neither **can** I.
Informal: *I do too. · I don't either. · Me too. · Me neither.*
Note the difference: **So it is / So I did** (subject before the auxiliary) is not agreement but **confirmation**, often with mild surprise: *A: It's freezing. B: So it is!*

## British do after modals
British English allows **do** after a modal: *A: Are you going? B: I might **do**. · I haven't seen it, but I should **do**.* This is not used in American English.

## Common mistakes
- ~~Do you like it? — Yes, I like.~~ → Yes, I **do**.
- ~~I can't swim and neither I can.~~ → ...and neither **can** I.
- ~~A: I'm tired. B: So I do.~~ → So **am** I.
structure:
## Что остаётся после опущения
| Оригинал | Короткий вариант |
|---|---|
| can swim | ... but he can. |
| has finished | ... but she has. |
| is working | ... but I am. |
| works / worked | ... but he does / did. |
| should have phoned | ... but I should have. |
| might have been waiting | ... she might (have). |

## Согласие
| Утверждение | Согласие | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| positive | So + aux + S | So do I. · So is she. |
| negative | Neither / Nor + aux + S | Neither can he. |
| разг. | I do too. / I don't either. | Me too. · Me neither. |

## Подтверждение
| Форма | Значение |
|---|---|
| So + S + aux | «Да, так и есть» — So it is! |

## Формулы
> **S + aux**, but **S + aux** (контраст)  ·  **So + aux + S**  ·  **Neither + aux + S**
> В конце предложения: **I have** (не I've), **he is** (не he's).

exercises.title: Оставьте только вспомогательный

items.text: He hasn't been to Japan, but I {{have}}.
She said she would call, and she {{did}}.
I don't like jazz, but my husband {{does}}.
A: Are you tired? B: No, I'm not, but Sam {{is}}.
They didn't arrive on time, but we {{did}}.
My sister doesn't speak Spanish, but her friend {{does}}.
I can't drive, but my sister {{can}}.
A: Was the film good? B: It {{was}}, actually. I was surprised.

exercises.example: I can't swim, but Tom (can / does). → ... but Tom **can**.

exercises.title: so, neither, nor
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужное слово (вспомогательный глагол или neither / nor).

items.text: A: I love hiking. B: So {{do}} I.
A: I haven't seen it. B: Neither {{have}} I.
A: She's very talented. B: So {{is}} her brother.
He can't cook, and {{neither|nor}} can I.
A: I'd like to travel. B: So {{would}} I.
A: I didn't enjoy it. B: {{Neither|Nor}} did I.
She hasn't called, and {{neither|nor}} has her sister.
I wasn't invited, and {{neither|nor}} was Tom.

items.q: A: Have you finished? B: Yes, I ___.
items.why: На конце предложения вспомогательный не сокращается: **I have**.

items.q: A: Is she coming? B: I think she ___.
I didn't tell anyone, but I wish I ___.
items.why: Сожаление о прошлом: **I wish I had** (= told).

items.q: A: You haven't been to Rome. B: No, but my wife ___.
A: Didn't you lock it? B: Yes, I ___.
She isn't a nurse, but her sister ___.
Какой вариант НЕверен? A: Have you met Anna? B: ...
items.why: В конце предложения *have* не сокращается: ~~Yes, I've~~.

items.q: A: I can't hear a thing. B: ___
A: It's freezing! B: ___ (подтверждаю, чуть удивлён)
items.why: **So it is** — подлежащее перед вспомогательным значит подтверждение.

items.q: She's never been to Spain, but ___.
A: I don't like olives. B: ___

answers: I haven't seen the film, but Dan has.
I have not seen the film, but Dan has.

items.prompt: She doesn't eat meat, but her husband eats meat.
answers: She doesn't eat meat, but her husband does.
She does not eat meat, but her husband does.

items.prompt: I didn't go to the meeting, but my colleague went to the meeting.
answers: I didn't go to the meeting, but my colleague did.
I did not go to the meeting, but my colleague did.

items.prompt: He isn't tired, but I am tired.
answers: He isn't tired, but I am.
He is not tired, but I am.

items.prompt: A: I love Italian food. B: (Согласитесь, используя so.)
answers: So do I.

items.prompt: A: I haven't been to London. B: (Согласитесь, используя neither.)
answers: Neither have I.
Nor have I.

exercises.instruction: Переведите на английский. Ключевые слова даны.

items.prompt: Я не умею готовить, и он тоже. (cook)
answers: I can't cook, and neither can he.
I can't cook, and nor can he.
I can't cook, and he can't either.
I can't cook and neither can he.
I cannot cook, and neither can he.

items.prompt: Она сказала, что поможет, и помогла. (help)
answers: She said she would help, and she did.
She said she'd help, and she did.
Yes, I have.
Yes I have.

items.prompt: — Мне нравится этот город. — Мне тоже.
answers: So do I.
I do too.

items.prompt: Он не пришёл, а должен был. (should)
answers: He didn't come, but he should have.
He did not come, but he should have.

I have, actually. I went to Turkey last year.
